output:
Congrats on the wedding, Sizwe. First job tonight: **take the key out and don’t crank it again.** You’ve already driven it and tried starting it a few times, so pump or injector damage is possible—but it’s not automatically a R40,000 write-off. We need to inspect it first.

Kobus means well, but that’s old Land Rover advice. A modern common-rail diesel pump relies on diesel for lubrication; topping up won’t fix the petrol already in the system. **Don’t drive it. Get it towed** and have the pump and injectors checked before anyone starts it again.

If they’re okay, draining the tank, flushing the lines, fitting a new fuel filter and bleeding it is usually around **R2,500–R4,500**. Can’t promise the total until it’s inspected. Check your insurance policy for roadside towing before paying a tow guy cash.

My shop in Umbilo is open Saturday 7–12. Thabo can drain it first thing. One customer managed this twice in the same year at the same garage; we made him a sticker for the fuel flap. In my first year as an apprentice, 1995, I put diesel in the boss’s Golf. He still tells that story at every braai, so you’re in good company.

And borrow a bakkie for the sound system and cake anyway—don’t plan the wedding around a drained tank. The cake has enough pressure on it already. Congrats, bru.
